## Proposed change
Migrate Airzone empty Unique IDs.
As reported in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/130536, it seems that Airzone devices connected via Ethernet instead of Wifi, report an empty MAC address on the WebServer (`mac: ""`).
This caused the integration to create Airzone entries with a Unique ID value of `""` and now we need to remove that Unique ID and set it to None.

pr_comments: Don't we have something better to set it to?

> Don't we have something better to set it to?

@joostlek unfortuntaly we don't, because the IP address + Port can't be used according to https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/entity_registry_index/#unacceptable-sources-for-a-unique-id
Do we have anything else? serial number? Is the normal airzone 1 config entry == 1 device? then we can use the config entry id

> Do we have anything else?

No, we don't.

> serial number?

No serial number exposed via API.

> Is the normal airzone 1 config entry == 1 device? then we can use the config entry id

We can have multiple devices on 1 config entry if it's a zonified installation.
Is there a way we can identify zones?

> Is there a way we can identify zones?

The only ID that we have for zones is the ID which is: [1, 32], with the first one being usually set to 1 and the following zones incremented accordingly.
We can have two entries with:
Entry #1
- 1 System
- 3 Zones -> 1, 2 and 3

Entry #2
- 1 System
- 1 Zone -> 1

> Is zone 2 always zone 2?

Not really, it depends on the configuration performed by the installer.
AFAIK, the IDs can be changed to whatever value [1, 32] for both systems and zones.

The configuration that I provided as an example is the typical one, but not necessarily the only possible one.
It's more like, having no unique id is a shitty user experience, so I'm trying to avoid it as much as possible. But we can have the zones have entry_id-zone_id.

> It's more like, having no unique id is a shitty user experience, so I'm trying to avoid it as much as possible. But we can have the zones have entry_id-zone_id.

Yeah, I agree with you, but there's nothing we can use as a unique ID for older Airzone devices.
That's why I requested Airzone to expose the WebServer API call with the MAC address, in order to be able to use it as a Unique ID. Unfortunately, older devices won't be updated so there won't be an unique ID for them...

BTW, I believe that your suggestion (`entry_id-zone_id`) is the default unique ID used right now since we always do: `self._attr_unique_id = entry.unique_id or entry.entry_id`.
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/a047abd51088ae60e54ce423371f47f3b52cc3f3/homeassistant/components/airzone/entity.py#L181
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/a047abd51088ae60e54ce423371f47f3b52cc3f3/homeassistant/components/airzone/binary_sensor.py#L190
So there's no need to change that.

Why did we have that in the first place if we expected all devices had a mac address lol

Also, what is the config entry unique id set to?

> Why did we have that in the first place if we expected all devices had a mac address lol

Not all devices had a MAC address, only the ones with the WebServer API call functionality.
The bug is caused on those devices with the WebServer API call functionality which return an empty MAC.
Devices without the WebServer API call functionality aren't affected and don't have an unique_id set (not even "").

> Also, what is the config entry unique id set to?

In those devices with the WebServer API call functionality returning an empty MAC address it's set to "" (which is a `\0`).

The users affected by this issue have already removed the integration and added it again.
Therefore, the fix isn't needed anymore.

issue_context.title: Airzone integration: There are multiple airzone config entries with the same unique ID.
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have two Airzone Units in my home with separate IP's, controlling separate hardware.
Today under Settings I noticed a new error appearing which states:
> There are multiple airzone config entries with the same unique ID.
> The config entries are named 'Airzone 192.168.28.45:3000', 'Airzone 192.168.28.46:3000'.
> To fix this error, [configure the integration] and remove all except one of the duplicates.
>> Additional error is: This stops working in version 2025.11.0. Please address before upgrading.

I deleted both Airzone units from HA, then "Rebooted the system".
Once HA restarted I added the Airzone integration, then added both Airzone units.  After a moment in time the above error returned.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.11.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Airzone

Hi @rc5kamps,

It seems that your WebServer is returning an empty "mac" address value ("") and the integration is setting "" as the unique ID of both devices.
I will fix it in a future version, but in the meantime can you check if there's a newer firmware for your devices on the Airzone Cloud app?

Thanks Noltari,
I reached out to the vendor asking if they can perform a remote firmware upgrade.  Once complete, I will try again, and update you with the results

Hi Noltari,
I just upgraded both of our AirZone AirDoo devices from firmware version 6.15 to the latest which is 10.12/6.20.
I then removed both AirZone systems from HA, rebooted HA, then reinstalled.
The good news is with this upgrade, the above error has not returned.

Thus it seems if others have this same issue, then please upgrade to the latest firmware version.

Thanks again for your quick attention to this issue!

> Hi Noltari, I just upgraded both of our AirZone AirDoo devices from firmware version 6.15 to the latest which is 10.12/6.20. I then removed both AirZone systems from HA, rebooted HA, then reinstalled. The good news is with this upgrade, the above error has not returned.

That's great :)
I'm sorry that you had to remove the entries and add them again :_(

Anyway, try to check for updates from time to time because the Airzone staff is fixing a lot of issues :)
